notes:
The whole list is on n140.jpg (printed page 129, running head "IRISH COAST."). n139.jpg is page 128: the end of the report text, signed by Alexander G. More and Richard M. Barrington, 19th May, 1885. n141.jpg is page 130: the List of Birds noticed. Neither has any rows of this list. The list's heading is "List of Light-stations." The column heads read, as rotated text, "Spring." and "Autumn", then "Miles from shore." and "Names of Observers". There is no heading for the station column and no column for light characters, so character is null throughout. The page has no sub-headings, so coast holds the page's running head.

How I filled the fields:
- Printed: The dot leaders are shortened. The reply marks are copied as printed: x, o and dashes (–). Fractions are written as ½. Italics are shown with underscores. The only italic text is "No replies." (rows 2, 26 and 34). "No schedule sent." is in roman type.
- Number: "5.*" and "8.*" are recorded as "5*" and "8*". The asterisk is part of the number, so it isn't repeated in marks.
- Marks: "brace" marks the three rows whose two-line observer entries are joined by a curly brace (5*, 7 and 27).
- Keepers: Names are split at "and" or commas. Each name's final full stop is dropped, but abbreviations such as "Wm." and "Robt." are kept.
- Other: This holds the Spring and Autumn reply marks, the miles from shore, and "No replies." / "No schedule sent."
- Old Head: The row is split as name "Old Head", place "Kinsale, Cork". You could treat "Old Head, Kinsale" as the name instead.
- Directional labels: For Eagle Island E./W., Slyne Head N./S. and Arran Island N./S., the label goes with the name, because it is set off by a comma. Oyster Island's "N. Sligo" has no comma, so it is recorded as the place (presumably North Sligo).
- Type: This appears only as "Lt.-ship", for rows 5*, 6, 8, 8* and 10. Tuskar Rock (7) has no type.
- "do." (ditto): For rows 6 and 7 it stands for Wexford. For row 8* it stands for Wicklow.

Printed as such (copied, not corrected):
- "ArklowSth.Lt.-ship,Wicklow" (row 8) is printed with no spaces.
- "JohnRedmond" (row 27) is printed with no space; the keeper is recorded as "John Redmond".
- Odd spellings, kept as printed: "Howth Baily" (usually Baily), "Innishtrahull" (usually Inishtrahull), "Arranmore", "Arran Island", "Barrels Rock" (no apostrophe), "Valentia", and "Michael Cunniam" (perhaps for Cunningham).
- "Joseph Hill" is given for both 22 Killybegs and 23 Oyster Island. This could be one man or a printer's repeat.

Numbering:
- There is no No. 9; 5* and 8* appear instead.
- No. 35 is missing: the list goes from 34 to 36.
- That makes 40 rows. Four say "No schedule sent." (4, 18, 31, 36), which leaves 36 schedules sent, as the footer says.

My counts match the footer ("Spring, 36 schedules sent out; replies received, 27. Autumn, 36 schedules sent out; replies received, 26."): 27 x marks in Spring and 26 in Autumn.

Where the image corrects the OCR:
- Row 1 is "Fastnet" (the OCR garbles it).
- Row 5*'s observers are "Patrick Cullen and William Clydesdale" (OCR "Wallisan Clydesdale").
- Row 7 is "Richard Hamilton and Patrick D'Arcy" (missing from the OCR).
- Row 16's observer is "W. H. James".
- Row 27 is "John Redmond, J. Young and R. Lyons".
- Row 32 is "Thomas Fortune" (OCR "lortune").
- Row 37 is "Tearaght" (OCR "Learaght").
- Rows 13, 30 and 31 are 3 miles (OCR "8").
- Rows 36 and 40 are ½ mile (OCR "i" and "4").
